notable_absence.finding: No RBAC role named for --add/--remove, which create/destroy a schedule-and-policy object referenced by live repositories. Also notable: the plan --get example output ('Description: This plan does a backup every hour and merge 6 hours as well as at the end of the week ... Default: False') shows a Default: False field for the built-in _daily plan in the --get output, while the --list example table shows Default: True for the same _daily plan two examples earlier in the same page - a direct internal inconsistency between two worked examples on the same reference page for the same named plan, exactly the kind of unreviewed copy-paste slip the authorship-provenance hypothesis predicts.

cross_component_finding: This page resolves the round's central open question precisely as framed: couchbase-cli backup-service plan DOES manage a plan object end-to-end (list/get/add/remove, with a --task JSON schema carrying name/task_type/full_backup/merge_options/schedule fields), which at first glance looks like it contradicts the prior finding that 'cbbackupmgr has no plan equivalent.' It does not contradict it - it COMPLICATES it usefully: couchbase-cli and cbbackupmgr are different binaries. cbbackupmgr (the archive-native backup/restore tool) genuinely has no plan/schedule/PRUNE vocabulary, confirmed again by this page's own --task schema comment restricting task_type to only BACKUP or MERGE ('it can be either BACKUP or MERGE') - PRUNE is absent here too, on the Backup-Service-facing CLI, not just on cbbackupmgr. So the precise, corrected statement for reconciliation is: the Backup Service's plan/task object (BACKUP/MERGE/PRUNE) is manageable from TWO surfaces - the REST API directly, and this couchbase-cli backup-service plan wrapper around that same REST API - while cbbackupmgr remains the one Couchbase CLI with no plan concept at all. Additionally, this page's merge_options.offset_start/offset_end (nested under 'merge_options', task-add time) is a THIRD spelling of the already-logged two-way merge-offset field-name mismatch (merge_offset_start/merge_offset_end on backup-service.md's plan overview vs. top-level offset_start/offset_end on backup-trigger-merge.md's immediate-trigger endpoint) - worth flagging to reconciliation as a three-way, not two-way, field-name inconsistency for backup:merge-offset.
